purpose: Adds a two-tier (command vs interactive) rate limiting system to the Probot app — per-repo hourly, per-user daily, per-PR cooldown, and a shared daily token budget — persisted in a new rate_limits table in the learning store (SQLite/Postgres/MySQL + JSON fallback), with gated admin /rate-limits and /rate-limits-reset commands and RATE_LIMIT_* env overrides.
riskRationale: Implementation is well-structured, parameterized, and unusually well-tested (mock + real store-backed e2e suites), but the check-then-record flow is non-atomic so concurrent webhook events can overshoot every limit, the per-PR cooldown lookup omits the repo dimension causing cross-repo false denials, the documented space-separated --repo/--user reset syntax silently performs a GLOBAL reset, and command-tier limits with 429 comments are applied to auto-triggered pr.opened/pr.synchronize reviews. The store failure path also fails open, and the token budget is charged only from fixed estimates. No critical security or correctness bugs found.
breakingChanges: Rate limiting defaults to enabled:true, so existing deployments immediately throttle slash commands, conversations, replies, and auto-reviews (10/hr per repo, 50/day per user, 500k token/day) and will see new 'Rate Limit Reached' comments
New rate_limits table and four indexes auto-migrate into the learning-store schema on next startup (idempotent)
Two new slash commands (/rate-limits, /rate-limits-reset) gated behind rateLimiting.adminUsers (empty by default, so dead until configured)
New RATE_LIMIT_* env overrides added to config; AgentConfig now requires the rateLimiting field (buildConfig() and DEFAULT_CONFIG include defaults)

text: Comprehensive and well-engineered rate-limiting feature: a clean RateLimiter core in lib over a minimal RateLimitStore contract, a thin consistent app-side helper, schema-validated env config, gated admin commands, and strong unit plus real store-backed e2e test coverage. The main gaps before merge are the non-atomic check-then-record flow (bursts bypass every cap), the repo-less per-PR cooldown key (cross-repo false denials), the admin reset flag-parsing bug that silently performs a global reset, and command-tier throttling + misleading 429 comments applied to auto-reviews; several minor accuracy, logging, and dead-code nits remain.

reasoning: The cross-repo cooldown bug and the admin reset fallthrough are concrete functional bugs, and the check-then-record TOCTOU window plus estimate-only token accounting weaken the exact cost-runaway protection this PR targets. These require an interface-wide signature change and a reserve-at-check-time redesign that are not safe as one-click automated fixes, so the PR needs another revision.

message: Clean, single-source-of-truth RateLimiter class over a minimal RateLimitStore contract: all four limit types are enforced in one place with a consistent RateLimitResult, the disabled path returns early without recording, and the 429 message includes a precise reset time.

Tests go beyond pure mocks: a comprehensive mock-store suite covers every limit, reset, cleanup, and disabled path, plus a separate real end-to-end suite exercises the actual SQLite-backed LearningStore (record, count, token sums, last-time, aggregation, reset, cleanup).

All new rate-limit SQL is fully parameterized (no injection surface), uses ISO-8601 UTC timestamps consistently with the JSON fallback, and the schema migration ships targeted indexes matching actual query patterns.

Admin commands are correctly gated behind rateLimiting.adminUsers (safe empty default), use postOrUpdateComment with a marker to avoid comment accumulation, and the reset logic uses parameterized deletes.

TOCTOU race: checkReview() reads current usage, then the expensive LLM run executes (often minutes), then recordReview() persists usage only after it completes (and only on success — on a thrown error no row is written). Because the EventBus runs subscribers concurrently (SUBSCRIBER_CONCURRENCY=10, Promise.allSettled) and GitHub delivers webhooks in parallel, a burst of /review, /fix, or @mention triggers can all pass the check before any usage is recorded, exceeding reviewsPerRepoPerHour, reviewsPerUserPerDay, the per-PR cooldown, and the daily token budget by up to the concurrency factor. Failed or empty runs never count toward limits, so repeated failing attempts consume no quota. This re-opens the exact cost-runaway hole the PR is meant to close.
suggestion: Reserve capacity at check time: insert a 'pending' rate_limits row (charged the tier estimate) immediately after an allowed check and reconcile it (update tokens_used / mark completed, or back it out) after the run, so concurrent requests are counted before execution begins. Treat reservations as consumed quota since failed runs still spent tokens; at minimum record in a finally-style path so failed attempts count.

message: getLastRateLimitTime() filters only by (pr_number, tier), never by repo. PR/issue numbers are scoped per repository, so an action on PR #42 in repo A sets the cooldown for PR #42 in repo B (and issue #42 in the same repo), deterministically blocking legitimate command/interactive actions on unrelated PRs. The JSON fallback has the identical defect (json-db.ts:1089), so both enforcement backends are affected.
suggestion: Thread repo into the cooldown lookup: change the RateLimitStore interface to getLastRateLimitTime(repo, prNumber, tier), update both SQL/JSON implementations to filter by repo, and pass repo through the LearningStore facade and the RateLimiter.checkReview call site (rate-limiter.ts:146).

message: The FLAG_PATTERN (command-match.ts) only captures a value after '='. The documented space-separated form `/rate-limits-reset --repo <name>` parses --repo as boolean true (verified: flags.repo === true), so repoFlag/userFlag resolve to undefined and the code falls through to `if (allFlag || (!repoFlag && !userFlag))` => resetAll(), wiping every rate-limit record app-wide instead of the targeted repo/user. Only the --repo=name equals-form works; a bare /rate-limits-reset also resets globally.
suggestion: Reject value-less flags and require explicit scope: treat a boolean-valued --repo/--user flag as invalid syntax, never fall through to resetAll() on an unrecognized flag, and either default a flag-less reset to the current event's repo or refuse with a usage message.

message: The command-tier limit (and its 429 comment) is applied to pr.opened and pr.synchronize auto-reviews as well as /review commands, even though the PR scopes the command tier to slash commands. The actor is attributed to the sender/pusher via extractActor, so one active contributor pushing frequently can exhaust their per-user daily quota and block auto-reviews on unrelated PRs, and once a repo hits 10/hr a 'Rate Limit Reached' comment is posted on a PR where nobody invoked the bot — silently degrading a configured auto-review feature.
suggestion: Decide deliberately whether auto-reviews are in scope. If cost control includes them, at minimum skip the misleading 429 comment for non-comment-triggered events (or gate it behind a config flag); alternatively only enforce command-tier limits on comment-invoked /review commands.

message: recordRateLimit() accepts tokensUsed but none of the 8 subscriber call sites pass it, so the daily token budget is always charged the fixed per-tier estimate (25k command / 5k interactive). A single large review/fix run can consume far more than 25k real tokens, so actual spend can drift well above the advertised 500k/day budget without tripping the limiter — the budget is effectively a proxy for action count.
suggestion: Thread real token usage from the run results (the engine already exposes usage) into recordRateLimit and pass it to recordReview, falling back to the tier estimate only when actuals are unavailable.

message: Every denied request posts a brand-new comment via postComment (no upsert). A user repeatedly re-triggering a blocked command, or a burst of denied events, accumulates a stack of 'Rate Limit Reached' comments — each an extra GitHub API call, so the denial path itself can be spammed on a public repo.
suggestion: Use postOrUpdateComment with a stable marker (like STATUS_MARKER in admin.ts) so repeated denials update a single rate-limit notice instead of appending new comments.

message: The LearningStore facade fails open: when the store is unavailable, countRateLimitActions() returns 0, sumRateLimitTokens() returns 0, and getLastRateLimitTime() returns null, so every check passes and rate limiting silently disables — the exact cost-runaway scenario this control exists to prevent. This matches the codebase's graceful-degradation convention, but for a cost-control mechanism the guardrail disappears exactly when there may be an infrastructure problem.
suggestion: For a security/cost control, consider failing closed on the rate-limit read paths (deny when the store cannot measure usage) or at least surface a loud, repeated warning and cache last-known counts so limits don't silently vanish. At minimum log at error level when rate-limit reads fall back.

message: RateLimitTier is declared identically in three places (types/index.ts:370, learning/types.ts:46, utils/rate-limiter.ts:8), a drift risk if a tier is added or renamed in only one module. Separately, rateLimiting was added to PromptConfig/PromptConfigSchema 'for parity' though the app never reads it — documented but dead config surface.
suggestion: Define RateLimitTier once (e.g. in lib/src/types/index.ts) and re-export it from the other two modules; drop rateLimiting from PromptConfigSchema unless it will actually be consumed from .opencode-reviewer.yml.

message: getStatus() maps getRateLimitUsageByRepo() (which counts rows across all tiers) against reviewsPerRepoPerHour, the command-tier-only limit, so the '/rate-limits' 'Per-Repo Hourly (command tier)' section can show over-limit counts that are never actually enforced. The `remaining` field for allowed results also ignores token-budget headroom.
suggestion: Filter getRateLimitUsageByRepo to tier='command' when building the status (matching enforcement) or relabel the section as 'all tiers', and include token-budget headroom in the computed `remaining` value.

message: The startup rate-limit cleanup failure is logged via console.warn, while the rest of the codebase uses the structured Logger utility — inconsistent, non-structured output that bypasses log-level formatting.
suggestion: Create a Logger instance (e.g. const logger = new Logger('RateLimiter')) and use logger.warn(...) instead of console.warn.

message: RateLimiter is imported as a value from @opencode-pr-agent/lib but never referenced in the file (only createRateLimiter is used, and its result is implicitly typed). Dead import.
suggestion: Remove RateLimiter from the import statement.

message: The admin gate uses a case-sensitive exact match: adminUsers.includes(author). GitHub usernames are case-insensitive, so an admin configured as 'Alice' is silently denied when commenting as 'alice', and non-admins are rejected without any diagnostic feedback.
suggestion: Normalize both sides to lowercase before comparing, e.g. adminUsers.some((u) => u.toLowerCase() === author.toLowerCase()).

message: AutoAnalyzeSubscriber runs a full /analyze LLM pipeline when an issue labeled needs-analysis is opened, but it is not rate limited — the one LLM-spending path left completely unguarded by this PR. Abuse requires a maintainer-applied label, so it is a gap rather than an open vector, but it is the same cost-runaway concern the PR addresses.
suggestion: Wire checkRateLimit/recordRateLimit into AutoAnalyzeSubscriber (command tier, targeting the issue number) mirroring FixSubscriber's label-triggered handling, or explicitly document it as intentionally exempt.

message: A review_comment.created that is both a threaded reply (has in_reply_to_id) and contains @opencode-reviewer is handled by both ReplySubscriber and ConversationSubscriber, each running its own LLM call and each recording its own rate-limit action — one user message is double-counted against the per-user daily limit and token budget and costs two expensive calls. The dual-fire pre-dates this PR, but the new rate-limit recording doubles the charge.
suggestion: Have one subscriber defer when the other will clearly handle the event (e.g. skip ReplySubscriber when the body contains the mention handle), so a single user message triggers one LLM call and one rate-limit record.

message: parseEnvInt() has no bounds checks, so env overrides like RATE_LIMIT_REVIEWS_PER_REPO_HOUR=-5 or a huge value bypass the min/max validation in RateLimitingConfigSchema (buildConfig() never runs the zod schema). A negative value makes the repo hourly limit always deny; a huge value disables it.
suggestion: Clamp parsed values to the same bounds used in the schema (e.g. Math.max(0, Math.min(1000, parsed))) in the rateLimiting section of buildConfig().

message: The admin allow-list is read from buildConfig() inside the handler instead of the config passed to registerSubscribers, so a deployment that configures adminUsers programmatically (not via env) silently disables the admin commands while the limiter itself was built from the passed config — two config sources can disagree.
suggestion: Pass the resolved AgentConfig into createAdminSubscriber (as the other subscribers' config is resolved once at registration) and read adminUsers from it for consistency.

message: recordRateLimitAction pushes a row and calls this.save(), which serializes the entire JSON database to disk on every rate-limited action — under sustained command traffic the JSON fallback backend rewrites the whole file on each action.
suggestion: Debounce/batch saves (e.g. save once per event loop tick or on close), or accept this cost since the JSON backend is a degraded fallback.

message: No app-level tests cover the new rate-limit helpers (checkRateLimit/recordRateLimit) or AdminSubscriber; the reset-all fallthrough bug and the unbounded 429-comment posting above would have been caught by a small unit test.
suggestion: Add tests for handleReset flag parsing (including the '--repo name' space form), admin allow-list gating, and that a denied check posts the 429 comment only once per window.
